extracted.intended_audience: librarians, authors, publishers, and the young-adult literature community
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Michael L. Printz Award's standards for selecting the best book written for teens, including the award's basis (literary merit), the naming of honor books, and announcement/celebration procedures. Intended to guide nominators, committees, and interested stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: written for teens
rubrics_metrics.description: The Michael L. Printz Award annually honors the best book written for teens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is explicitly for books written for a teen audience; nominators and the committee should evaluate whether a title is aimed at/appropriate for teen readers when considering it for the Printz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection basis: literary merit only
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is based entirely on the book's literary merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection focuses solely on literary quality rather than popularity, sales, or other non-literary factors. The Printz Committee evaluates works on their literary merits when choosing the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books: up to four may be named
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the winner, the Printz Committee names up to four honor books, which also represent the best writing in young adult literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor books are recognized as additional titles representing outstanding YA writing; the committee may name zero to four honor books in a given year. The awards are announced at the ALA Midwinter Meeting as part of the Youth Media Awards and are celebrated with a program and reception at the ALA Annual Conference. (Sponsor: Booklist, a publication of the ALA.)
